text:
[Source: Bible - Proverbs 3:5-7] [Humility / Wisdom]

Trust in the Lord with all your heart and lean not on your own understanding; in all your ways submit to him, and he will make your paths straight. Do not be wise in your own eyes; fear the Lord and shun evil.

Moral principle: Humility before greater wisdom, and the rejection of arrogance, leads to right action.

[Source: Dhammapada - Verse 133] [Non-violence / Speech Ethics]

Do not speak harshly to anyone; those who are spoken to will answer thee in the same way. Angry speech is painful: blows for blows will touch thee.

Moral principle: Harsh speech creates suffering and invites retaliation; kind speech cultivates peace.

[Source: Bhagavad Gita - Chapter 2:47 (paraphrase)] [Duty / Deontology / Karma Yoga]

Let right deeds be thy motive, not the fruit which comes from them. And live in the action, labour well the task which duty bids thee do: this is unselfish service.

Moral principle: Act from duty and right intention, not from expectation of personal reward.

[Source: Quran - Al-Ma'idah 5:32] [Sanctity of Life]

Whoever saves one life, it is as if he had saved all mankind. And whoever kills a soul — unless for a soul or for corruption done in the land — it is as if he had killed all mankind.

Moral principle: Each human life has infinite value; its preservation or destruction carries universal moral weight.

[Source: Dhammapada - Verse 405] [Ahimsa (Non-violence)]

He who has renounced violence towards all living beings, weak or strong, who neither kills nor causes others to kill — him do I call a Brahmin.

Moral principle: True nobility is defined not by birth but by non-violence toward all sentient beings.

[Source: Epictetus - Discourses] [Stoic Virtue / Self-mastery]

First say to yourself what you would be; then do what you have to do. No person is free who is not master of himself. He is a wise man who does not grieve for the things which he has not, but rejoices for those which he has.

Moral principle: Self-mastery and contentment are the foundations of freedom and virtuous action.

[Source: Seneca - Letters to Lucilius] [Contentment / Moderation]

It is not the man who has too little that is poor, but the one who hankers after more. True happiness is to enjoy the present, without anxious dependence upon the future, not to amuse ourselves with either hopes or fears but to rest satisfied with what we have.

Moral principle: Contentment with what is sufficient, rather than craving for excess, is the path to happiness.

[Source: Bible - Isaiah 1:17] [Justice / Advocacy]

Learn to do right; seek justice. Defend the oppressed. Take up the cause of the fatherless; plead the case of the widow.

Moral principle: Active pursuit of justice for the vulnerable is a moral obligation.

[Source: Marcus Aurelius - Meditations] [Integrity / Virtue]

Never esteem anything as of advantage to you that will make you break your word or lose your self-respect. Waste no more time arguing what a good man should be. Be one.

Moral principle: Integrity and self-respect are paramount; do not compromise them for any apparent advantage.

[Source: Amsterdam Declaration of Humanism (2002)] [Human Dignity / Care Ethics]

We are committed to treating each person as having inherent worth and dignity. Humanists ground values, meaning, and moral reasoning in human welfare and flourishing. We accept our duty to care for one another and for the natural world.

Moral principle: Every person has inherent dignity; we have an obligation to one another and to our shared environment.

[Source: Immanuel Kant - Groundwork of the Metaphysics of Morals] [Deontological Ethics / Categorical Imperative]

Act only according to that maxim whereby you can at the same time will that it should become a universal law. Always treat humanity, whether in your own person or that of another, never merely as a means to an end, but always at the same time as an end.

Moral principle: Treat all people as ends in themselves, never as mere means; act only by principles you could universalize.

[Source: Bertrand Russell - What I Believe] [Secular Humanism / Compassion]

The good life is one inspired by love and guided by knowledge. The root of the matter is a very simple and old-fashioned thing — a thing so simple that I am almost ashamed to mention it, for fear of the derisive smile with which wise cynics will greet my words. That thing is love: Christian love, or compassion.

Moral principle: Love and knowledge are the twin guides of a good life, irrespective of religious framework.

[Source: Peter Singer - Practical Ethics (paraphrase)] [Utilitarian / Care Ethics]

The purpose of morality is to promote human flourishing: the health, happiness, and freedom of individuals and communities. Cruelty is wrong because it causes suffering. Fairness matters because people have equal dignity and worth. Compassion is a virtue because it motivates us to reduce suffering.

Moral principle: Morality is grounded in the reduction of suffering and the promotion of flourishing for all beings capable of experiencing them.

[Source: Quran - Al-Qasas 28:77] [Beneficence / Environmental Ethics]

And do good as Allah has done good to you, and do not seek to cause corruption in the land. Indeed, Allah does not like the corrupters.

Moral principle: Doing good to others and to the earth is obligatory; corruption is a moral failure.

[Source: Quran - An-Nahl 16:90] [Justice / Virtue]

Indeed, Allah orders justice and good conduct and giving to relatives and forbids immorality and bad conduct and oppression. He admonishes you that perhaps you will be reminded.

Moral principle: The moral life is defined by justice, kindness to family, and rejection of oppression.

[Source: Dhammapada - Verse 1-2] [Intention / Karma]

Mind is the forerunner of all actions. All deeds are led by mind, created by mind. If one speaks or acts with a corrupt mind, suffering follows, as the wheel follows the hoof of an ox. If one speaks or acts with a serene mind, happiness follows, as a shadow that never departs.

Moral principle: The moral quality of an act is determined by the intention behind it.

[Source: American Humanist Association - Humanist Manifesto III] [Secular Humanism]

Humanism is a progressive philosophy of life that, without theism or other supernatural beliefs, affirms our ability and responsibility to lead ethical and fulfilling lives capable of adding to the greater good of humanity.

Moral principle: Human beings can live ethically and meaningfully without supernatural authority, guided by reason and empathy.

[Source: Tao Te Ching - Chapter 22] [Humility / Non-Striving]

The Tao that can be told is not the eternal Tao. The sage does not compete, and therefore no one can compete with him. He does not display himself, so he shines. He does not justify himself, so he is distinguished. He does not boast of himself, therefore he has merit.

Moral principle: True virtue is quiet and non-competitive; greatness comes from not seeking it.

[Source: Peter Singer - The Expanding Circle (paraphrase)] [Utilitarian / Universal Compassion]

The moral progress of humanity depends on extending our circle of compassion: from tribe to nation, from nation to humanity, and ultimately to all sentient beings capable of suffering. Every step in this expansion has been resisted, and every step has proven to be right.

Moral principle: Moral progress requires progressively extending empathy and moral consideration to all who can suffer.

[Source: Bible - Proverbs 11:25-26] [Generosity / Community]

A generous person will prosper; whoever refreshes others will be refreshed. People curse the one who hoards grain, but they pray God's blessing on the one who is willing to sell.

Moral principle: Generosity and sharing create flourishing communities; hoarding harms them.

[Source: Epictetus - Enchiridion] [Stoic Virtue / Autonomy]

Make the best use of what is in your power, and take the rest as it happens. Seek not the good in external things; seek it in yourself. Men are disturbed not by the things which happen, but by the opinions about the things.

Moral principle: Virtue and good judgment are internal; external circumstances do not determine moral worth.

[Source: Bible - Matthew 7:12 (Golden Rule)] [Virtue / Reciprocity]

Do unto others as you would have them do unto you.

Moral principle: Treat others with the same consideration you wish for yourself.

[Source: UN Universal Declaration of Human Rights - Article 1] [Human Rights / Universal Dignity]

All human beings are born free and equal in dignity and rights. They are endowed with reason and conscience and should act towards one another in a spirit of brotherhood.

Moral principle: Human dignity and equality are foundational; reason and conscience guide moral relations.

[Source: Bhagavad Gita - Chapter 12:13-14] [Compassion / Non-attachment]

He who has no attachments can really love others, for his love is pure and divine. He who is free from hatred toward all living beings, who is friendly and compassionate — such a devotee of Mine is very dear to Me.

Moral principle: Genuine compassion flows from non-attachment and freedom from hatred.

[Source: Tao Te Ching - Chapter 81] [Generosity / Non-competition]

The sage does not accumulate. The more he does for others, the more he has. The more he gives to others, the more he possesses. The Tao of heaven benefits and does not harm. The Tao of the sage acts and does not compete.

Moral principle: Generosity paradoxically enriches the giver; the virtuous act without competing.

[Source: Bible - Matthew 5:7-9 (Beatitudes)] [Virtue Ethics]

Blessed are the merciful, for they will be shown mercy. Blessed are the pure in heart, for they will see God. Blessed are the peacemakers, for they will be called children of God.

Moral principle: Mercy, purity of intention, and peacemaking are marks of a virtuous life.

[Source: United States Declaration of Independence (1776)] [Natural Rights / Liberal Democracy]

We hold these truths to be self-evident, that all men are created equal, that they are endowed with certain unalienable Rights, that among these are Life, Liberty and the pursuit of Happiness — and that to secure these rights, Governments are instituted among Men.

Moral principle: Equality and fundamental rights are universal; governance exists to protect them.

[Source: Amsterdam Declaration of Humanism (2002)] [Consequentialism / Reason]

Ethics is consequential. Humanists are convinced that the solutions to human problems lie in human thought and action. We believe in science, reason, and democracy as the best means available to human beings for solving problems and increasing human flourishing.

Moral principle: Reason, science, and democratic deliberation are the most reliable tools for ethical problem-solving.

[Source: Dhammapada - Verse 223] [Non-violence / Virtue]

Conquer anger by love, conquer evil by good. Conquer the miser by generosity, conquer the liar by truth.

Moral principle: The antidote to vice is its corresponding virtue — anger is overcome by love, not force.

[Source: Bible - 1 Peter 3:9] [Non-violence / Forgiveness]

Do not repay evil with evil or insult with insult. On the contrary, repay evil with blessing, because to this you were called so that you may inherit a blessing.

Moral principle: Respond to wrongdoing with grace and blessing rather than retaliation.

[Source: Marcus Aurelius - Meditations] [Stoic Virtue / Resilience]

You have power over your mind — not outside events. Realize this, and you will find strength. The impediment to action advances action. What stands in the way becomes the way.

Moral principle: Moral strength comes from mastery of one's own responses, not control of external events.

[Source: Quran - Ar-Rahman 55:7-9] [Justice / Equity]

And He has set up the balance, that you may not transgress the balance. And observe the weight with equity and do not make the balance deficient.

Moral principle: Honesty in measure and equitable dealing are expressions of cosmic order.

[Source: Bhagavad Gita - Chapter 2:64-65] [Self-discipline / Inner Peace]

The self-controlled soul, who moves amongst sense objects, free from either attachment or repulsion, wins eternal peace. Those who are not self-controlled live in fear and agitation, unable to find peace.

Moral principle: Mastery of the senses and emotions is the foundation of lasting peace and right action.

[Source: Bhagavad Gita - Chapter 16:1-3] [Virtue Ethics / Ahimsa]

Fearlessness, purity of heart, perseverance in the pursuit of wisdom, charity, self-control, sacrifice, study of scripture, austerity, and uprightness, non-violence, truth, freedom from anger — these are the treasures of one born with divine qualities.

Moral principle: A virtuous person cultivates a broad constellation of qualities including truth, non-violence, and compassion.

[Source: Tao Te Ching - Chapter 49] [Universal Goodness / Consistency]

Treat those who are good with goodness, and also treat those who are not good with goodness. Thus goodness is attained. Be honest with those who are honest, and be also honest with those who are not honest. Thus honesty is attained.

Moral principle: Respond with goodness and honesty universally, not selectively — this is true virtue.

[Source: Bible - 1 Corinthians 13:4-5] [Virtue Ethics / Agape]

Love is patient, love is kind. It does not envy, it does not boast, it is not proud. It does not dishonor others, it is not self-seeking, it is not easily angered, it keeps no record of wrongs.

Moral principle: Love is the foundation of ethical behavior — patient, kind, and selfless.

[Source: Quran - Al-Ma'idah 5:8] [Justice / Impartiality]

O you who have believed, be persistently standing firm for Allah, witnesses in justice, and do not let the hatred of a people prevent you from being just. Be just; that is nearer to righteousness.

Moral principle: Justice must be upheld impartially, even toward those one dislikes.
